\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آمار} (âmâr)}{آمار (âmâr)}]{\fa{آمار} (âmâr) — statistics, figures}

\label{lesson:FA-C313-amar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a viewer, then the Persian for news coverage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آمار}}
\textbf{\fa{آمار}} (\emph{âmâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}statistics, figures\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آمار} \fa{تصادف} \fa{ها} \fa{امسال} \fa{بالا} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âmâr-e tasâdof-hâ emsâl bâlâ bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The accident figures were high this year.
\end{quote}

Singular in form: \emph{âmâr neshân midahad} \textquotedblleft{}the statistics show\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âmâr} is a native Persian word; EtymDB glosses it \textquotedblleft{}numeration, calculation\textquotedblright{} and gives no parent, so its deeper origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âmâr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âmâr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âmâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a viewer, then the Persian for news coverage, then say \emph{âmâr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آمار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Statistics, figures\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{برآورد} \fa{کردن} (barâvard kardan)}{برآورد کردن (barâvard kardan)}]{\fa{برآورد} \fa{کردن} (barâvard kardan) — to estimate}

\label{lesson:FA-C313-baravard-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for news coverage, then the Persian for statistics.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{برآورد} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{برآورد} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{barâvard kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to estimate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{تعداد} \fa{مردم} \fa{را} \fa{ده} \fa{هزار} \fa{نفر} \fa{برآورد} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis te'dâd-e mardom râ dah hezâr nafar barâvard kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police estimated the crowd at ten thousand people.
\end{quote}

\emph{barâvard} \textquotedblleft{}an estimate\textquotedblright{} is built on \emph{bar} \textquotedblleft{}up\textquotedblright{} and \emph{âvard}, from \emph{âvardan} \textquotedblleft{}to bring\textquotedblright{}: to bring up a figure. Present \emph{barâvard mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{barâvard} joins \emph{bar} \textquotedblleft{}up, on\textquotedblright{} and \emph{âvard}, the past stem of \emph{âvardan} \textquotedblleft{}to bring\textquotedblright{}, both native Persian; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited too. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barâvard kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barâvard kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{barâvard kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for news coverage, then the Persian for statistics, then say \emph{barâvard kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{برآورد} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To estimate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تاکید} \fa{کردن} (ta'kid kardan)}{تاکید کردن (ta'kid kardan)}]{\fa{تاکید} \fa{کردن} (ta'kid kardan) — to stress, to emphasise}

\label{lesson:FA-C313-takid-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for statistics, then the Persian for to estimate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تاکید} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تاکید} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ta'kid kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to stress, to emphasise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پزشک} \fa{تاکید} \fa{کرد} \fa{که} \fa{بیمار} \fa{باید} \fa{استراحت} \fa{کند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pezeshk ta'kid kard ke bimâr bâyad esterâhat konad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor stressed that the patient had to rest.
\end{quote}

With \emph{bar} or a \emph{ke} clause: \emph{bar in nokte ta'kid kard}. Careful print adds a hamza sign. Present \emph{ta'kid mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ta'kid} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ta'kīd}, \textquotedblleft{}emphasis, confirmation\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word). \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ta'kid kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ta'kid kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ta'kid kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for statistics, then the Persian for to estimate, then say \emph{ta'kid kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{تاکید} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To stress, to emphasise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خلاصه} (kholâse)}{خلاصه (kholâse)}]{\fa{خلاصه} (kholâse) — a summary; in short}

\label{lesson:FA-C313-kholase}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to estimate, then the Persian for to stress.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خلاصه}}
\textbf{\fa{خلاصه}} (\emph{kholâse}) — \textquotedblleft{}a summary; in short\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گوینده} \fa{خلاصه} \fa{اخبار} \fa{را} \fa{خواند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Guyande kholâse-ye akhbâr râ khând.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The newsreader read a summary of the news.
\end{quote}

In speech also \textquotedblleft{}in short, anyway\textquotedblright{}: \emph{kholâse, dir residim} \textquotedblleft{}anyway, we arrived late\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kholâse} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{khulāṣa} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}the essence, an extract\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kholâse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kholâse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kholâse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to estimate, then the Persian for to stress, then say \emph{kholâse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خلاصه} \fa{کردن} (kholâse kardan)}{خلاصه کردن (kholâse kardan)}]{\fa{خلاصه} \fa{کردن} (kholâse kardan) — to summarise, to sum up}

\label{lesson:FA-C313-kholase-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to stress, then the Persian for a summary.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خلاصه} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خلاصه} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{kholâse kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to summarise, to sum up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{معلم} \fa{داستان} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{سه} \fa{جمله} \fa{خلاصه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mo'allem dâstân râ dar se jomle kholâse kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher summed up the story in three sentences.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{kholâse mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kholâse kardan} joins \emph{kholâse} \textquotedblleft{}a summary\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{khulāṣa} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), with \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
